DerivedFunction.description:
The four ways code may reach a number the article did not write.

Each member's arithmetic is defined by the implementation of the same name in
`idhazh.derived_values`, and `inputs` is ordered because two of them read the
order: a share's part comes first and its whole follows.
DerivedFunction.title: DerivedFunction

DerivedValue.description: One number code computed, and the complete chain back to what it read.

bin_lower.description: The inclusive floor of the bin a count was taken over. Null off a histogram.
bin_lower.title: Bin Lower

bin_upper.description: The ceiling of that bin. Null off a histogram.
bin_upper.title: Bin Upper

function.description: Which of the four. Closed, and a name outside the list does not load.

inputs.description: Every Tier 1 element this value read, in the order the function reads them. Element ids and never another derived value: a chain that nests can be complete at each hop and still name no element at the bottom.
inputs.title: Inputs

source_unit.description: What a conversion moved from. Null on the other three.
source_unit.title: Source Unit

unit.description: What this value measures, which for a conversion is the target unit. Null on a count, because a count of things measures nothing.
unit.title: Unit

unit_table_version.description: The date-stamp of the table that said the two units measure the same thing. Null on the other three, because they read no table.
unit_table_version.title: Unit Table Version

value.description: What code computed, as a decimal pinned to text the way a Tier 1 value is.
value.title: Value

version.description: The date-stamp of the arithmetic that produced this value - the four functions and the binning rule. Stamped by code, so a later build can say whether this number would come out the same today.
version.title: Version

DerivedValue.title: DerivedValue

VisualEncoding.description:
Which marks fill which channel of the drawing.

One field per member of `EncodingRole`, in that order, mirroring
`PlanEncodings`. Every role is present and an unused one is empty, so "which
channels does this drawing use" is a question about which are non-empty
rather than about which are there - and a reader of this file learns the
same nine words it would learn from the plan.

bins.description: The quantity that is binned rather than plotted.
bins.title: Bins

category.description: The discrete axis: what each mark is.
category.title: Category

entity.description: Who or what a mark is about.
entity.title: Entity

quantity.description: The measured axis: how big each mark is.
quantity.title: Quantity

quantity_x.description: The second measured axis, where a type has two.
quantity_x.title: Quantity X

series.description: What splits the marks into groups.
series.title: Series

size.description: The third channel, drawn as area.
size.title: Size

VisualEncoding.title: VisualEncoding

VisualMark.description:
One thing the drawing puts on the page, and where it came from.

A mark is one entry in one channel - a bar's name or a bar's length, never
both halves of a bar. That is what lets a channel have a length of its own,
and a channel with a length of its own is the only way a drawing can be
caught holding four names and three figures.

**Every mark states its provenance and exactly one kind of it**, the same
rule `DisplayedValue` holds: the Tier 1 element whose own characters or own
figure it draws, or the derived value with its complete chain back to
several of them. Written as two optionals with no rule, a mark that came
from nowhere is a payload somebody can write.

derived.description: The arithmetic and its chain, where no single element states the figure drawn. Null on a mark cut straight out of the article.

element_id.description: The Tier 1 element this mark was cut from. Null on a derived mark.
element_id.title: Element Id

mark_id.description: How the encoding below addresses this mark. Unique within one visual.
mark_id.title: Mark Id

text.description: What a naming mark says: the element's own characters, cut and sanitized where the trust boundary was crossed. Null on a mark that measures rather than names.
text.title: Text

unit.description: What `value` measures. Null on a naming mark, and null on a count, which measures nothing.
unit.title: Unit

value.description: How big a measured mark is, as a decimal pinned to text the way a Tier 1 value is. Null on a mark that names rather than measures.
value.title: Value

VisualMark.title: VisualMark

VisualType.description:
The full declarable vocabulary of forms a plan may ask for.

Declarable is not renderable. A type with no compiler template can be named
by a plan and is deterministically downgraded to its nearest built
neighbour, which is how the planner says which template is worth building
next. What may reach a reader is gated elsewhere; what may be named is here.
VisualType.title: VisualType

changelog.change: Initial shape: the marks with their values and provenance, the encoding.
changelog.why: The reader's browser draws the chart, so it needs the marks rather than an SVG.

description:
One published visual: its marks, its channels, its type and what draws it.

Published at `frontend/public/digest/<YYYY>/<MM>/<DD>/<item_id>.json`, beside
the day payload that points at it. **The shard is the day directory**, which
is what every other published store uses and what a reader fetches. The chart
data is kept out of `digest.json` because the day payload is never deleted,
so anything inside it would be undeletable and `retention.image_months` would
have nothing to act on (owner, 2026-09-13).

encoding.description: Which marks fill which channel. Every role a key, an unused one empty.

item_id.description: The story this drawing belongs to, and the stem of this file's own name.
item_id.title: Item Id

marks.description: Every figure and every name the drawing puts on the page.
marks.title: Marks

renderer_version.description: The date-stamp of the drawing contract this data was compiled for. The page refuses a version it does not know, so a later change that would move pixels cannot redraw an older day without saying so.
renderer_version.title: Renderer Version

type.description: The form the drawing takes. A type the drawing code does not know is refused rather than approximated - a chart that is nearly the plan is a chart nobody asked for.
